function: Learned 3D CNN only detects blocked antennas from the power delay profile; beam healing is greedy or codebook selection, not learned; no area applies (p. 8, 10)
notes: Excluded under function; reasons 1 to 4 do not apply (research article, proposes methods, a CNN is a proposed learned component acting on physical-layer power delay profiles). The only learned element is the 3D CNN that outputs a per-antenna blockage mask (p. 8: "spatial distribution of blockages using the power delay profiles"), scored by blocked-antenna identification error and confusion matrices (p. 12-13). The paper separates blockage detection from channel estimation (p. 2: "[22] is channel estimation rather than blockage detection,") and says its mitigation avoids re-estimating the CSI (p. 14: "its efficiency: it does not require re-estimation of the full"). The mitigation (greedy antenna selection, convex sparse beamformer, codebook) is not learned (p. 10, 14), so the learned method solves none of the problems of areas 1 to 7. Borderline: if the reviewer reads the PDP and blockage-mask estimation as channel estimation (area 2), the marks would be q1 0 (own spherical-wave simulator, p. 4, 10), q2 0 (not stated), q3 0 (only non-learned heuristic [53] and Neyman-Pearson [38] baselines, p. 12), q4 0 (qualitative complexity only, p. 13), q5 0 (no code or data link).
